$comment: Food-label vocabulary, mapped to element ids. A label does not speak this game's language: it says Skim Milk, Live Cultures, Mineral Salt (Calcium Citrate), where the game says milk, bacteria, calcium. This file is that translation and nothing else — it never invents an element, it only says which existing one a phrase means. An entry whose target id does not exist is an error, and tools/validate.mjs says so.
$rules: Keys are lowercase, punctuation-stripped. Longest key wins, so 'locust bean gum' is tried before 'gum'. Values are element ids. A value of null means the phrase is deliberately recognised as UNRESOLVABLE — see $vague.
$vague: Some label phrases are legally permitted to hide what they mean. 'Natural flavours' can be any of thousands of compounds and the label is not required to say which. Mapping those to null lets the reader say so out loud rather than silently dropping them, which is the honest answer and a more interesting one.

vague.natural flavours: The law lets this stand for any of thousands of compounds, and does not require the label to say which.
vague.natural flavour: The law lets this stand for any of thousands of compounds, and does not require the label to say which.
vague.natural flavors: The law lets this stand for any of thousands of compounds, and does not require the label to say which.
vague.artificial flavours: A blend the maker is not required to itemise.
vague.flavouring: A blend the maker is not required to itemise.
vague.flavour: A blend the maker is not required to itemise.
vague.spices: Any mixture of spices; the label need not break it down.
vague.herbs: Any mixture of herbs; the label need not break it down.
vague.vegetable gums: A thickener class, not a single thing — the specific gums are usually named in the brackets after it.
vague.emulsifier: A class of additive, identified on most labels only by a number.

$near: A label phrase whose element the game HAS, but which is not that element — calcium citrate contains calcium, it is not calcium. The reader says which, rather than quietly claiming an identity that would be false.
